newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Normandy says qtly gold production a record.
newsitem.headline: Normandy says qtly gold production a record.

text.p: Gold miner Normandy Mining Ltd said on Thursday group production rose to a record 410,102 ounces in the quarter to June 30, for annual 1996/97 production of 1.515 million ounces.
Group quarterly production was up from 363,662 ounces in the March quarter, Normandy said.
Production attributable to Normandy rose to 342,534 ounces, up 2.6 percent on the March quarter, while the average cash cost of production fell 2.4 percent to A$325 an ounce.
The average cash cost for the year came in at A$336 an ounce, down A$30 an ounce on the previous year.
Normandy, which will release its annual results on August 20, said it sold 373,397 ounces of gold in the June quarter at an average realised A$598 an ounce.
Normandy chairman Robert de Crespigny repeated forecasts of a record 1996/97 profit, driven by a 9.8 percent fall in gold cash costs and an increase in zinc shipments and realised price.
Gold sales in 1997/98 would continue to be protected by hedging, de Crespigny said in a statement.
Normandy had forward sold 5.7 million ounces of gold an average A$720 an ounce, and expected an average realised gold price of A$610 an ounce, he said.
Zinc concentrate shipments for the June quarter rose to a record 82,250 tonnes, up from 49,391 tonnes in the March quarter.
Normandy said the formation of the Big Bell/Cuddingwarra joint venture in Western Australia continued its strategy of improving the cash cost of production.
Attributable production was expected to fall by about 30,000 ounces a year, but a net aggregate pre-tax profit boost of A$30 million was expected over the next four years.
Normandy shares were one cent firmer at A$1.37 at 10.20 a.m. (0020 GMT) in an overall weaker market.
